scope: Production build on the local Apple M2 with Playwright 1.63.0. Model inference ran on this Mac, not on a remote service. Normal browser profiles at a 390x844 viewport; WebKit also uses mobile and touch mode.
observed_failures: The previous published app returned to the fixed Hello, daydream. demo after a reload during naming and lost the four generated library entries. Reproduced with the worker protocol fixture against commit 78f05ec.

Real WebKit naming completed four titles on WebGPU, then its worker teardown crashed the page on reload or worker shutdown. Native reports identified EXC_BAD_ACCESS in WebCore::GPUDevice::contextDestroyed via InspectorInstrumentation. Normal session disposal, queue completion, GPUDevice.destroy and device.lost did not resolve that reproduction.
The physical iPhone failure was not directly observed; its exact cause is not established by the Mac reproduction.

changes.cache: Page-owned storage with 4 MiB ArrayBuffer blocks in IndexedDB, chunked Cache API fallback, verified commit manifests, immutable revision keys, legacy cache reads, incomplete-write cleanup and bounded memory fallback. A denied IDB read does not skip the backup store.
changes.library: Save each complete score and partial title before optional inference. Restore validated scores on reload; merge title changes by stable ID without replacing notes or shrinking the batch. Recover interrupted jobs on pagehide/pageshow.
changes.naming: Remember the last 64 titles across batches and reloads; reject copied examples and near-duplicates; try twice and then use an explicitly recorded measured-character fallback.
changes.browser_policy: Safari/WebKit, including iOS browser shells, uses local CPU inference for both models to avoid the reproduced GPU teardown crash. Chromium/Gecko retain GPU selection. Older Safari without WebGPU uses the matching plain WASM runtime.
changes.memory: Dispose the optional title pipeline after each batch and load its next instance from persistent model storage.

cache_regression_scope: 18 MiB plus 73-byte fixture under a simulated 4 MiB storage-entry cap
Exact bytes after reload and browser restart in all three engines
Worker storage blocked while page-owned storage remains usable
Cache API fallback when IndexedDB is blocked or denied
Failed readback never reports a saved model
Aborted partial downloads are not cache hits
Legacy cache reuse and quota failure handling
library_regression_scope: Four-song batches retain identities and exact RTTTL musical bytes during naming
Partial, invalid, failed and cancelled title responses retain all scores
Reload during naming restores complete scores and partial titles without restarting models
Explicit pagehide/pageshow persisted events cover late manifest completion, terminated melody workers, partial names and restartable controls
real_multisong_invariants: IDs, song count and exact RTTTL musical bytes unchanged by naming
Second batch completes while all model and runtime requests are blocked
No repeated title across two four-song batches

scope: Melody reuse within the tab and after reload
Optional title model cached in multiple committed blocks and reused with model networking blocked
Real melody generation using a non-fallback hardware WebGPU adapter

limitations: No physical iPhone was available. These are Mac browser-engine tests, not a guarantee for every iOS release or device.
The GPU teardown diagnosis is from automated WebKit runs; the CPU policy is a compatibility workaround.
Private browsing, storage eviction, full storage or clearing site data can still require downloads. Storage failures are reported instead of promising persistence.
The smaller title model can produce weak suggestions; two of 24 titles in the recorded multi-song tests used the explicitly marked fallback.
Model files are cached; the site shell still needs to be reachable after reload.
The updated title model needs its own initial download; the previous model files are not usable as this model.
